item.title: NEW: Critical Fortinet FortiMail Zero-Day Exploited for RCE
item.description:
Headline: Critical Fortinet FortiMail Zero-Day Exploited for RCE

Summary:
Fortinet has disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-104286, in its FortiMail secure email gateway. The flaw, which has a CVSS score of 9.8 and is under active exploitation, allows an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files, leading to remote code execution. CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating urgent action from federal agencies. While patches are pending, Fortinet has provided immediate workarounds, including disabling the IBE feature or restricting web access to the management interface.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Patch Management

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: A critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-104286) in Fortinet FortiMail is being actively exploited. The flaw allows unauthenticated RCE. Patches are pending.

item.description:
Headline: KillSec Ransomware Group Dismantled in International Takedown

Summary:
A coordinated international law enforcement operation, dubbed 'Operation KillSwitch,' has successfully dismantled the prolific KillSec ransomware group. The operation, led by German authorities with support from Europol, resulted in the seizure of the group's servers, its dark web leak site, and 110 terabytes of stolen data. Investigators have identified the suspected main operator as a 16-year-old, and several arrests have been made across Europe.

Headline: China-Aligned Group TA419 Targets U.S. AI Policy Experts

Summary:
A China-aligned cyber-espionage group, tracked as TA419 by Proofpoint, is conducting sophisticated phishing campaigns targeting U.S. experts in artificial intelligence policy. The attackers use elaborate impersonations of prominent officials and AI company employees to build rapport before luring targets to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing sites. The goal is to steal cloud account credentials, including passwords, MFA codes, and session cookies, to gather intelligence on U.S. AI strategy.

item.description:
Headline: Ransomware Data Exfiltration Surges 275%, Zscaler Reports

Summary:
A new report from Zscaler ThreatLabz highlights a dramatic shift in ransomware tactics, with the volume of exfiltrated data increasing by over 275% year-over-year to nearly 900 terabytes. This indicates a strategic move from encryption-focused attacks to data theft for extortion. The report also notes that attackers are increasingly targeting employees in privileged roles and using generative AI to accelerate their operations. The freight & logistics and utilities sectors saw the largest growth in attacks.

Severity: Informational

Categories: Threat Intelligence, Ransomware, Data Breach

Article Type: Report

item.title: UPDATE: Citrix Patches Two Critical NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Attack
item.description:
Headline: Citrix Patches Two Critical NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Attack

Summary:
Citrix has released emergency patches for eight vulnerabilities in its NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances, with two critical zero-days, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, confirmed to be under active global exploitation. The flaws allow for unauthenticated remote code execution, leading to potential webshell deployment and full network compromise. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added both vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating immediate patching and compromise investigation for federal agencies. The attacks were reportedly underway for weeks prior to disclosure, with attackers gaining persistent access to internal networks. Organizations are urged to apply updates immediately and hunt for indicators of compromise, as patching alone does not remediate existing intrusions.

Severity: Critical

Summary:
Two major third-party risk incidents emerged, highlighting supply chain vulnerabilities. The U.S. Department of Defense disclosed a significant data breach from October 2025 that affected the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) through a third-party provider, compromising sensitive personnel data. Separately, secure file transfer company Kiteworks took the drastic step of advising a customer-wide shutdown on September 25 based on 'credible, imminent' federal threat intelligence. item.title: NEW: NetScaler Zero-Days CVE-2026-88771 & CVE-2026-88772 Actively Exploited
item.description:
Headline: NetScaler Zero-Days CVE-2026-88771 & CVE-2026-88772 Actively Exploited

Summary:
Citrix has disclosed two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, in its NetScaler appliances, which are being actively exploited in the wild. The vulnerabilities, both rated with a CVSS score of 9.5, can lead to denial of service or remote code execution. Threat actors have been observed exploiting these flaws since at least August 21, 2026, to deliver web shells, establish initial access, and maintain persistence. Unit 42 analysis identified over 50,000 exposed NetScaler instances and detailed two distinct attack patterns, one involving a crafted DTLS packet and another using a three-stage log poisoning technique to achieve RCE. Immediate patching is critical.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Report

Reading Time: 8 minutes

item.title: UPDATE: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Actively Exploited in the Wild
item.description:
Headline: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Actively Exploited in the Wild

Summary:
Unit 42 has issued a threat brief concerning two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, affecting Citrix NetScaler devices. Both vulnerabilities have been assigned a CVSS v4.0 base score of 9.5 and are confirmed to be actively exploited in the wild. According to telemetry from Palo Alto Networks Cortex Xpanse, over 50,000 NetScaler instances are exposed and potentially vulnerable globally. Organizations are urged to apply the latest security updates from Citrix immediately. The advisory warns that patching alone will not remove existing compromises, and recommends that organizations hunt for signs of post-exploitation activity. While specific TTPs have not been released, general threat hunting guidance is provided.

Severity: Critical
